# MM-P3-L4-RR01 — Maintenance manual - Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1
Revision: Rev F (This revision supersedes Rev E)
Plant: P3, line P3-L4
Equipment: EQ-P3-L4-RR01

Scope
This document provides maintenance instructions, rationale, and acceptance criteria for the Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) at Plant P3, line P3-L4. It is intended for trained maintenance engineers and technicians responsible for preventive maintenance, corrective repairs, and inspection activities on the mill. Related documents: SB-1028, SOP-P3-L4-02, SOP-P3-L4-03. Follow site lockout/tagout and hot-work procedures as directed in SOP-P3-L4-02 and SOP-P3-L4-03.

Background and purpose
The radial ring rolling mill at Heat Treat performs high-force deformation operations that rely on precise clamping and well-lubricated bearings. Failures in the mandrel clamp or main roll bearings can cause dimensional rejects, unexpected downtime, and safety hazards. This manual documents the essential maintenance tasks and the engineering rationale behind them, focusing on actions that influence part quality and machine reliability.

Key specification references
- The mandrel clamp bolt torque for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) is 605 N·m.
- The main roll bearing lubrication interval for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) is 135 hours.
These values are the controlling specifications for clamp integrity and bearing lubrication. Do not substitute alternative values without documented engineering approval referenced in SB-1028.

Tools
Recommended tools and consumables for tasks described below:
- Calibrated torque wrench sized to achieve specified mandrel clamp bolt torque
- Bearing grease gun compatible with bearing fittings
- Manufacturer-approved grease as specified in SB-1028
- Inspection mirror and strong portable light source
- Clean lint-free rags and approved solvent
- Fastener retention compound as specified in SB-1028
- Maintenance log forms and digital entry device for records
Only use tools that are calibrated and traceable per site calibration procedures. If replacement tools are used, record calibration status in maintenance records.

Procedure
General notes
- Perform all work with the mill fully de-energized and isolated per SOP-P3-L4-02. Verify isolation and document the verification.
- Use appropriate personal protective equipment and follow SOP-P3-L4-03 for hot surface and handling precautions.
- Clean work areas and components prior to inspection to avoid false indications.

Mandrel clamp bolt torque verification and adjustment
1. Prepare the clamp assembly by cleaning bolt threads and seating surfaces with approved solvent.
2. Inspect bolts and clamp components for wear or damage. If physical defects are present, remove the bolt and tag it for replacement per SB-1028.
3. Using the calibrated torque wrench, apply torque to each mandrel clamp bolt to the specified value: 605 N·m. Apply torque in a controlled manner and follow the clamp pattern to ensure even seating.
4. Where specified by SB-1028, apply fastener retention compound to the bolt threads after torque verification. Note: follow product cure guidance per SB-1028.
5. Record each bolt torque application in the maintenance log, including bolt identifier, operator initials, and any deviations.
Rationale: Controlled clamp torque ensures consistent mandrel seating and minimizes runout that can affect part geometry and bearing loads.

Main roll bearing lubrication
1. Verify bearing lubrication fittings are clean and free of contamination.
2. Using the approved grease and a properly primed grease gun, apply lubricant to each bearing fitting until slight purge of old lubricant is observed, or until bearing housing level indicates adequate fill as described in SB-1028.
3. Adhere to the controlling lubrication interval: The main roll bearing lubrication interval for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) is 135 hours. Record the timestamp of lubrication and the operating hours counter state in the maintenance log.
4. Inspect seals and housings for leaks during lubrication. If leaks are detected, tag the bearing assembly for repair and follow corrective procedures in SB-1028.
Rationale: Consistent lubrication reduces friction, heat, and wear, extending bearing life and maintaining dimensional stability of rolled rings.

Inspection and corrective actions
- Bearings: If abnormal noise, vibration, or leakage is observed, remove the bearing assembly for teardown and evaluation per SB-1028. Preserve bearing identification and condition photos for root cause analysis.
- Clamp bolts: Replace bolts that show thread damage, elongation, or surface defects. Use replacement parts and installation practices qualified in SB-1028.
- Records: Photograph critical conditions and attach to the corrective maintenance report.

Examples and scenarios
Example: If an operator reports increased roll vibration that coincides with torque verification showing a clamp bolt below specification, retorque all clamp bolts to 605 N·m and perform bearing lubrication. Log actions and monitor vibration per SOP-P3-L4-02. If vibration persists, escalate to engineering and initiate bearing inspection per SB-1028.
Example: During a routine lubrication, if heavy contamination is observed in the grease purge, sample the lubricant, note the contaminant description, and initiate bearing teardown and contamination analysis as specified in SB-1028.

Records to keep
Maintain the following records in the document control system and on the equipment maintenance history:
- Torque application log entries showing bolt identifiers, 605 N·m application confirmation, date, and technician initials.
- Lubrication entries documenting adherence to the 135 hours interval, grease type (as per SB-1028), amount applied, date, and technician initials.
- Inspection reports, photographs, and any nonconformance records generated during maintenance.
- Corrective action reports with root cause and disposition referencing SB-1028.

Acceptance criteria
The maintenance activity is acceptable when all of the following are met:
- Mandrel clamp bolts are torqued to the required value and show no physical defects or looseness after installation: 605 N·m applied and recorded.
- Main roll bearings have been serviced with the approved lubricant and the lubrication event is documented in accordance with the 135 hours interval.
- No abnormal noise, vibration, or leakage is present after return to service; if any abnormal condition remains, a documented corrective action and re-inspection plan must be in place per SB-1028.
- Maintenance records are complete and stored per SOP-P3-L4-02 and SOP-P3-L4-03.

References
SB-1028
SOP-P3-L4-02
SOP-P3-L4-03
